verdict.rationale: Sentry's Trace Explorer is documented to let you explore span samples, visualize span attributes, and aggregate data with flexible queries and filters, and the Issues page supports filtering by properties such as impacted users. That is the product's own ad-hoc group/filter capability over attributes. However, nothing documents behavior on high-cardinality fields like user or request IDs, or confirms that no pre-aggregation or index definition is needed. missing for 10: explicit evidence of group-by on high-cardinality fields (user id, request id), documentation that arbitrary attributes are queryable without pre-defined indexes or pre-aggregation, independent or hands-on corroboration of query performance at high cardinality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can group and filter by high-cardinality fields (user id, request id) without pre-aggregating or defining indexes first

citations.quote: You can explore span samples, visualize span attributes, and aggregate your data with flexible queries and filters.
This page allows you to filter by properties such as browser, device, impacted users, or whether an error is unhandled.
